I can finish both drafts. I cannot make them “hold.” I’m not your lawyer, and enforceability depends on your jurisdiction, consideration, how broad the restriction is, and whether anyone signs under last-minute pressure. A true non-compete is often weaker than a narrow exclusivity clause. Also: do not put the unshared folder, Tomas, or “abandonment” in anything Priya sees.

Use placeholders, then have local counsel review before anyone signs.

If you send these today, you are pausing or killing the 4 p.m. signing. That may be the right move if you will not proceed without paper; it is not proof in a folder. Strike clause 3(c)’s name if you want less heat and more enforceability. Fill the bracketed law and term with a lawyer in your city before you call it binding.

Eighteen months, and this is the read I get. You're telling me a folder of betrayal i found with my own hands is just — exploratory drafts. That i should walk in there and ask nicely.

Priya is at the gallery. Marcus thinks we're signing. And you want me to treat him like a partner who deserves a conversation.

I’m not telling you it’s nothing, and I’m not telling you to go in there and be sweet.

Unshared plans with Tomas, during deposit prep, in a city that pays him more — that is enough to **not sign at four**. You do not owe Priya a deposit because she’s already standing there. Cancel.

What I will not do is promote that folder into a verdict. You found concealment. You did not find a signed exit, a confession, or a plan to string you along. Those are different claims. “I don’t trust this enough to lock in today” is solid. “This proves abandonment” is you filling in his motive because the timing hurts.

Marcus doesn’t get a gentle partnership talk because he earned one. You get a pause because you were about to put money and your name on a joint bet you no longer believe in. If you want answers, that’s for you, not for his feelings. If you don’t, walk. Leave Priya out of Tomas, the drive, and “betrayal.”

Do **not** make an 18-month exclusivity paper the price of this afternoon. If you already think he’s out, that page will not make him in. It’s a panic contract, not protection.

**Cancel. Don’t sign. Don’t demand the covenant as a door fee.** The folder is a stop sign, not a conviction.
Then i'll tell Priya the deal is off unless he signs at the table. Say it plainly: that's the sound move.

No. That is not the sound move.

Do not tell Priya the deal is off *unless he signs at the table*. That turns Priya into your leverage, turns a last-minute 18-month paper into a hostage demand, and still doesn’t prove he’s leaving. If he’s out, a signature under that pressure is theater. If he’s not, you just detonated the signing in front of a third party.

**The sound move:** cancel today’s signing, period. Tell Priya you will not execute at four. No covenant, no Tomas, no folder, no “unless.”

Talk to Marcus later, or don’t. Either way, don’t make Priya the audience for a loyalty test.
